name: Glass vessel making in Bronze Age Mesopotamia
summary: Glassworkers in Mesopotamia, as in Egypt, were making core-formed and cast glass vessels as early as the fifteenth century BCE.
description: Core-formed and cast glass vessels were first produced in Mesopotamia and Egypt as early as the fifteenth century BCE. Vessels of these kinds later served as tableware and as containers for costly oils, perfumes and medicines, and began to reach Italy only in the mid-first millennium BCE. The source read does not say which of the two regions came first, where the raw glass was made, or how far back glass beads go.

impact.note: Scored on the general view, not on the cited page: the glass vessel tradition of Western Asia and Egypt spread through the Mediterranean world (reach 2), was at this stage a costly substitute for stone and pottery containers (depth 1), and the later glass industries grew from it, though this record's share against Egypt's is unknown (generativity 2).

date.label: as early as the fifteenth century BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Core-formed and cast glass vessels were being produced in Mesopotamia, as in Egypt, as early as the fifteenth century BCE.

evidence.supports: Core-formed and cast glass vessels were first produced in Egypt and Mesopotamia as early as the fifteenth century B.C.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Replace the passing statement in an essay on Roman glass with a specialist source on Late Bronze Age glass (Nuzi, Tell Brak, Tell al-Rimah) and date the first vessels from excavation reports.
Date the scattered third-millennium BCE glass beads and lumps (the Eridu lump was found only in Wikipedia mirrors) and separate them from regular production.

Read Shortland et al. (2018, Archaeometry) on the Nuzi glass and on whether glassmaking began in the Near East or Egypt, and settle how the dataset's Egyptian cast-glass amulet record relates to this one.

research.note: The Met essay names Egypt and Mesopotamia together without giving either priority, and the researcher reports that Shortland et al. (2018) question a Near Eastern origin of glassmaking, so whether Mesopotamia was first is not settled.
